title: API 570 Training in Corpus Christi: Piping Exam Prep Online
description: API 570 piping inspector exam prep for Corpus Christi: self-paced online study with instructor Q&A, built around unit piping, CUI, CMLs and dock lines.
h1: API 570 Training in Corpus Christi, TX: Piping Inspector Exam Prep for Unit, Rack and Dock Piping on the Coastal Bend
html:
API 570 exam prep for piping inspectors in Corpus Christi

Walk any unit on the Corpus Christi Ship Channel and most of what you pass is pipe: crude charge and overhead lines, hydrotreater effluent, amine and sour water circuits, steam and condensate, flare headers, and the racks that carry product to the docks. Add the B31.3 process piping of an LNG export terminal and an ethane cracker across the bay, and the Coastal Bend has more in-service piping per inspector than most places in the country. API 570 is the certification for the people who plan and judge the inspection of that piping.

Atlantis NDT's API 570 course is self-paced and online. You start the day you enrol, study when your shift pattern allows and put questions to an instructor whenever a B31.3 paragraph or an API 570 table refuses to make sense. There is no Atlantis classroom in Corpus Christi; everything is studied online. The American Petroleum Institute sets the eligibility rules, administers the piping inspector examination at Prometric test centres and issues the API 570 certificate, so each candidate applies to API directly, and the course is preparation for that examination rather than a route around it. Atlantis is not an API-approved training provider.

A piping-heavy coastline: where API 570 applies, and where it stops

API 570 covers in-service metallic process piping. Around Corpus Christi that takes in several quite different kinds of plant, each with its own inspection emphasis:

  • Refinery unit piping. EIA's January 2026 capacity list puts Valero's Corpus Christi refinery and Flint Hills Resources' Corpus Christi West plant at 290,000 barrels per calendar day each, with Flint Hills' East plant at 87,500. Their circuits run from ambient-temperature water lines to high-temperature sulfidation service, which spans most of the RP 571 mechanisms the exam lists.
  • Distillation-only plants. Buckeye Texas Processing and Magellan Processing, the latter now owned by ONEOK, run smaller crude and condensate units with no vacuum or coking capacity in EIA's list. Their piping is simpler, but overhead and exchanger circuits still corrode.
  • LNG process piping. Cheniere's Corpus Christi Liquefaction terminal in San Patricio County completed its Stage 3 expansion in August 2026, according to EIA, with two further midscale trains under construction. Its pre-treatment piping carries amine and water; its cold sections run in stainless and other low-temperature materials, where the exam's impact testing questions stop being abstract.
  • Petrochemical piping. Gulf Coast Growth Ventures, the ExxonMobil and SABIC complex in San Patricio County, pairs an ethane cracker with polyethylene and glycol units, and OxyChem runs a chemical plant at Ingleside. Caustic, quench water and cracked gas services bring their own circuits.
  • Dock and terminal piping. The Port of Corpus Christi says it owns 13 public oil docks while industry runs 16 private ones. The loading lines, manifolds and tank farm piping behind them are often in-plant piping that an API 570 inspector looks after.

Where API 570 stops matters on this coast because long-haul pipelines end here. Enbridge's Ingleside terminal alone takes crude from five lines, Gray Oak, Cactus I, Cactus II, EPIC and Harvest, and Flint Hills' Texas Pipeline System runs from Corpus Christi to terminals in Delmita, San Antonio, Austin, Waco and Dallas–Fort Worth. Transmission pipelines are governed by pipeline codes and federal pipeline regulations, not API 570, and the boundary between the two is set at each facility. The guide to the API 570 and pipeline code boundary explains how it is drawn, and why an inspector who works both sides of the fence must know which rulebook applies to the spool in front of them.

Corrosion under insulation on bay-side pipe racks

If one mechanism defines piping inspection on the Coastal Bend, it is corrosion under insulation. Warm, humid air, frequent wind off the water and heavy rain mean that once the jacketing on an insulated carbon steel line is damaged, water gets in and stays. Steam-traced lines, lines that cycle through the temperatures RP 571 identifies as most aggressive, and lines at supports and low points where water collects are the usual places to look first. Austenitic stainless lines at warm temperatures add the risk of external chloride stress corrosion cracking, because chlorides from the marine air and from the insulation itself concentrate on the hot surface.

For the exam, CUI is tested through API 570 itself, RP 571 and RP 574 rather than through the separate recommended practice on CUI. You are expected to know which piping is susceptible, how inspection extent is chosen once a visual survey has found damaged insulation, and which methods suit screening versus measurement. In the field, local teams combine insulation removal and UT with screening such as pulsed eddy current to decide where to strip; the guide to CUI in API 570 and API 510 inspection plans shows how it is written into a plan.

CML programmes: where Corpus Christi piping readings come from

Most piping inspection data on the ship channel starts as an ultrasonic thickness reading taken by a technician at a condition monitoring location. Circuits are drawn so that each one shares a material, a service and therefore a damage mechanism, and the CMLs on each circuit are placed where that mechanism is expected to act: elbows and tees for flow-driven thinning, the bottom of lines where water drops out, the first downstream fitting after a temperature change. API 570 calls these CMLs; older plant records may still say TMLs.

An API 570 inspector reads those numbers as a programme rather than a list. Long-term and short-term corrosion rates are compared for each CML, the governing rate is chosen, remaining life is calculated against the greater of the pressure design thickness and the owner's structural minimum, and the interval is the shorter of half the remaining life and the maximum for the circuit's piping class. When readings drift for no obvious reason, the inspector questions the data before the pipe: a probe placed on a different spot, a coating not removed or a gauge not calibrated for temperature can all fake a corrosion rate. The API 570 explainer and the corrosion rate guide go further.

Injection points and dead legs: a worked interval

Wash water into a crude overhead, neutraliser and inhibitor injection, caustic into crude charge: injection points are common in Coastal Bend refineries, and API 570 lets each one be treated as a separate inspection circuit, with a tighter maximum thickness interval. Here is the sort of question the exam builds from one.

A CML just downstream of a wash water injection nozzle read 0.310 in. three years ago and reads 0.280 in. today. The line's required thickness is 0.200 in.

  • Short-term rate: (0.310 − 0.280) ÷ 3 = 0.010 in. per year.
  • Remaining life: (0.280 − 0.200) ÷ 0.010 = 8.0 years, so half the remaining life is 4.0 years.
  • API 570's table sets a maximum thickness interval of 3 years for injection points, so the answer is 3 years, not 4.

Treat the same numbers as an ordinary Class 2 circuit and you would answer 4 years, half the remaining life and well inside that class's maximum. The question is really asking whether you noticed the words "injection point". The injection point guide covers how the circuit's limits are set upstream and downstream.

Dead legs are the other local favourite: bypasses, drains, sample points and spared lines where flow stops and water, solids or bacteria settle. API 570 asks for them to be identified and inspected, including the junction with the active line, and plants routinely remove the ones they no longer need. See dead leg inspection under API 570.

Studying API 570 on Coastal Bend rotations

A refinery inspector on a four-on, four-off rotation and a contract technician who disappears into a turnaround for weeks study in very different rhythms, and self-paced study accommodates both. Some habits work well here:

  • Read B31.3 as a PDF from the start. The open-book half of the exam gives you the code on screen, and B31.3 is long; knowing where Chapter V fabrication rules and the leak test paragraphs sit saves minutes per question.
  • Bring the field to the course. When you see an odd repair, a clamp or an unusual support detail on a rack, look up how API 570 and ASME PCC-2 treat it, and send the instructor your reading of the clause.
  • Keep a short list of the numbers you must know without the book: the piping classes and their maximum intervals, the injection point and soil-to-air rows, and the definitions the closed-book questions lean on.
  • Plan the exam window away from the turnarounds you expect, and leave slack for storm season, which runs June through November.

The exam windows and deadlines page lists the dates API has published; choose the window before you choose a study rhythm.

Getting to API 570 eligibility from a Corpus Christi job

API requires education plus piping experience within the last ten years, with a year of supervising or performing inspection inside it; the API 570 certification requirements page gives the full scale. Locally the starting points are fairly predictable.

  • UT thickness technicians working for inspection contractors build the most directly relevant experience, because CML surveys on process piping are inspection activity API recognises. ASNT certification for that work is covered on NDT training in Corpus Christi.
  • Del Mar College graduates from the Nondestructive Testing Technology or Process Technology associate programs at the Windward Campus may qualify for the two-year education line; API decides when it reviews the application.
  • Pipefitters and welders on repair and construction crews count fabrication and repair experience toward the longer routes, and need to add the year of inspection.
  • Engineers with a bachelor's degree, including graduates of Texas A&M University–Kingsville's engineering programs, need one year of piping inspection activity.

API 570, CWI or ASNT UT first? Sequencing credentials in Corpus Christi

Candidates often ask which certificate to chase first. On this coast the answer usually follows the work in front of you. On new LNG and petrochemical construction, welds are inspected to construction codes, and the AWS Certified Welding Inspector is the common credential; see AWS CWI exam prep in Corpus Christi. If you take the readings, your employer certifies you in UT under its own written practice to ASNT SNT-TC-1A. API 570 comes when you have the experience to judge in-service piping and set intervals. Many Coastal Bend piping inspectors hold all three, plus API 510, because a unit inspector who can cover vessels and the piping between them is easy to deploy.

Sponsoring API 570 candidates

Inspection contractors and owner-users regularly prepare small groups of piping candidates together, often UT technicians who have reached eligibility in the same year. A sponsored group can mix examinations, and fees are quoted on request. Each candidate applies to API personally, studies at their own pace and asks the instructor their own questions. Owners looking for NDE support on piping, rather than training, can see piping inspection services in Corpus Christi.

faq.q: Does dock and terminal piping at Ingleside count as API 570 experience?
faq.a: Often it does, because loading lines, manifolds and tank farm piping inside a terminal are commonly treated as in-plant piping rather than pipeline. The deciding factor is where the facility draws its code boundary and whether your work was inspection of metallic piping in service. Describe the circuits and your tasks accurately on the application; API reviews and verifies the experience you declare rather than accepting a job title.

faq.q: Can work on the Permian crude pipelines count toward API 570 eligibility?
faq.a: Experience on cross-country transmission pipelines is governed by pipeline codes, so it may not be accepted as the in-service process piping experience API 570 asks for. Station, terminal and facility piping that sits on the plant side of the boundary is a different matter. If most of your history is pipeline work, check the API 570 requirements carefully before applying, and consider whether a pipeline-specific credential suits your career better.

faq.q: Can I prepare for API 570 in Corpus Christi without a classroom?
faq.a: Yes, and with the Atlantis course there is no classroom to attend at all. You study online at your own pace, work through code lessons, calculations and timed practice papers, and send questions to the instructor when you are stuck. That fits refinery rotations, contract turnaround work and offshore hitches equally well. The exam itself is taken in person at a Prometric test centre once API has accepted your application.

faq.q: How does the course handle CUI and injection point questions?
faq.a: Both get their own lessons because both appear in the Body of Knowledge and both trip up experienced inspectors. CUI is taught through API 570, RP 571 and RP 574: susceptibility, inspection extent after a visual survey and method choice. Injection points are taught through the circuit definition and the interval table, with worked problems that hide the injection point inside the question so you learn to spot it.

faq.q: I take UT thickness readings for a contractor. How close am I to API 570 eligibility?
faq.a: That depends on your education. With a high school diploma API asks for three years of piping experience, including one year of supervising or performing inspection; with a two-year technology degree or certificate, two years. CML surveys on process piping are generally the kind of inspection activity API recognises. Count only experience from the last ten years, and keep records of the sites, circuits and dates you worked.

faq.q: Which edition of ASME B31.3 will my API 570 exam use?
faq.a: The one listed on the Publications Effectivity Sheet for the window you book. API publishes a Body of Knowledge and effectivity sheet for each set of windows, and editions change over time. Study from the edition on your sheet even if your plant works to another, because the exam is marked against the sheet. The course tells you which B31.3 paragraphs are in scope and which are excluded.

faq.q: Where do Corpus Christi candidates sit the API 570 exam?
faq.a: At a Prometric test centre. Prometric lists centres in and around Corpus Christi, and you pick one in its locator when you schedule, using the details API sends once your application is accepted. The exam is taken in person; there is no home or online sitting for API 570. Bring the identification Prometric requires and nothing else, since the code PDFs for the open-book half are provided on the computer.

faq.q: Can a Corpus Christi contractor enrol a group of piping inspectors together?
faq.a: Yes. Contractors often sponsor several UT technicians at once as they reach eligibility, sometimes alongside API 510 or API 653 candidates. Fees are quoted on request for the group. Every candidate receives an individual login, moves through the material at their own pace and asks their own questions, and every candidate applies to API separately.
